label: 2023 Women's European Volleyball Championship (CEV EuroVolley) - 33rd edition
hosts: Belgium, Italy, Germany, Estonia (Ghent, Verona, Monza, Turin, Dusseldorf, Tallinn, Brussels, Florence)
source: BUILT from cited bytes under WO-VB-1 (PLAN-VB). Capture: Wikipedia edition-page wikitext (action=raw), every match row citing its official CEV MatchStatistics report (unique per-row sources, IDs 66391-66435 pools / 68931-68938 + 67958-67965 finals; www-old.cev.eu, wayback-recoverable); infobox official match total 76 == built count. 24 teams, 4 pools of 6: A Ghent (host Belgium), B ITALY CITY-BY-DATE (Verona Aug 15 opener at the Arena di Verona, Monza Aug 16-19, Turin Aug 21-23 - venue table byte-mapped to every row), C Dusseldorf (host Germany), D Tallinn (host Estonia); R16+QF split Brussels/Florence per bracket lines; SF/3P/F Brussels. FIDELITY: per-team pool points-for/against recomputed from set tokens == wikitext standings spw/spl for ALL 24 teams. Spine R16->F exact. Champions TURKIYE - FIRST EuroVolley title (MVP Melissa Vargas, coach Santarelli): d. Italy 3-2 in the SF (15-6 fifth) then d. Serbia 3-2 in the Brussels final (13-15 from SRB side); Netherlands bronze 3-0 over Italy; top-3 (excl. already-qualified world champs Serbia) took the CEV berths to the 2025 World Championship - the qualification thread the tennis-style narrative preserves. Aug 15 - Sep 3 2023.
